text:
Ask. Then, the merchant's son Sudhana, who possesses the <term>bodhisattva</term> <gloss>enlightenment-being</gloss> qualities of overcoming obstacles and striving for complete purity, whose mind is made radiant by the light of the <term>bodhisattva</term> power, who is a steadfast <term>bodhisattva</term> possessing a heart that cannot be overcome or deterred by others, who is undaunted in mind by the excellent armor of <term>bodhisattva</term> vows, who strives to dwell in and fully develop the steadfast intention of a <term>bodhisattva</term>, who possesses the intention to fully grasp the rain of <term>bodhisattva</term> conduct, who possesses a mental continuum that is never satisfied by the rain of the <term>bodhisattva</term> teachings, who is manifest in the prayers to engage in all the virtues of a <term>bodhisattva</term>, who desires to fully dedicate himself to gathering all beings by transforming their paths, and who desires to rescue all beings from the great wilderness of <term>samsara</term> <gloss>cyclic existence</gloss>, and who is never satisfied with seeing, listening to, and serving spiritual friends, and who possesses the capacity to generate immeasurable offerings of the <term>dharma</term> <gloss>teachings</gloss>, bowed his head to the two feet of the monk Sudarshana <note>original: "bLta na sdug pa"</note>. Having circumambulated the monk Sudarshana hundreds of thousands of times to the right, and having looked at him again and again, he departed from the presence of the monk Sudarshana.

<summary>This passage describes the spiritual qualities of the merchant's son Sudhana and his respectful departure from the monk Sudarshana after seeking his guidance.</summary>
<keywords>Sudhana, Sudarshana, bodhisattva, dharma, samsara, spiritual practice, devotion</keywords>
